units.source_text: 从此以后，应该说我是活着的。

en.t: From then on, I suppose it should be said that I was alive.

units.source_text: 不可思议的却是一种不吉利的思绪随之与日俱增，仿佛明天就会死到临头。

en.t: What was strange, however, was that an ominous thought grew stronger day by day, as if death would come for me tomorrow.

units.source_text: 我祷告：但愿在我烧金阁之前，死神能放过我。

en.t: I prayed: may the god of death spare me until before I burn the Golden Pavilion.

units.source_text: 我决不生病，也没有生病的征兆。

en.t: I absolutely would not fall ill, and there was no sign of illness either.

units.source_text: 然而让我活着的各种条件的调整及其责任，一无遗漏地压在我一人的肩头上，我日益强烈地感觉到它的重量。

en.t: Yet the adjustment of all the conditions that kept me alive, and the responsibility for them, pressed without exception on my shoulders alone, and day by day I felt their weight more keenly.
